units.note: upstream interpolates a JS array of 10000 "a" strings (each element becomes its own argument); encoded compactly as a raw value of 10000 space-separated words, which yields the same 10000 arguments to echo

units.upstream: synchronous write errors in nested command substitutions
units.note: test.if(isLinux): /dev/full makes write(2) fail with ENOSPC synchronously; upstream runs it in a bun subprocess and checks stdout/exitCode (re-entrancy guard crash regression)

units.upstream: synchronous write errors in sequential statements
units.note: test.if(isLinux); every `|| echo fN` runs only because its /dev/full write failed

template: echo a > /dev/full || echo f1; echo b > /dev/full || echo f2; echo c > /dev/full || echo f3; echo d > /dev/full || echo f4

cases.note: extra: the failing builtin write itself has a non-zero exit (Bun 1.4.2 reports the odd code 65508, i.e. -ENOSPC truncated to u16; the builtin cat path reports 28)

units.upstream: builtin cat completing on a synchronous write error leaves the shell usable
units.note: test.if(isLinux); upstream runs three sequential $ commands in one bun subprocess with BUN_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_SHELL_BUILTINS=1 (enables the builtin cat; that flag must be in the Bun process env, so here cat may be the external /usr/bin/cat, which prints "cat: write error: No space left on device" on stderr, while the builtin cat prints nothing). Each command is one case.

template: echo hello | cat > /dev/full; echo again | cat > /dev/full; echo next | cat
cases.note: the two failing writes and the final `echo next | cat` in one script: the shell stays usable
